Repo: d:\_ntu台大\futureclass_未來教室\_dev\FutureClassroom — a .NET 10 backend (FutureClassroom.Api + FutureClassroom.Core + FutureClassroom.Job with Hangfire) + Next.js 16/React 19 frontend, PostgreSQL via EF Core. This is a planning task — do not write any code, just produce a detailed implementation plan as your response text.

## Goal (3 requirements from the product owner, in Chinese, already discussed with them):
1. 登入後只顯示該學生有選的課 / 該老師上的課 (After login, only show courses the student is enrolled in / courses the teacher teaches)
2. 學生第一次登入時去後端執行 job 撈選課紀錄 (On a student's first login, trigger a backend job that fetches their course selection record)
3. 學生可以登入本系統查看該課的分析結果,依學生最終的選課結果為主 (Students view analysis results scoped to their FINAL course selection result — i.e. after add/drop period ends)

## Confirmed facts from the product owner (already answered in conversation, do not re-ask):
- The "選課結果" (course selection result) comes from NTU's 新課程網 (Course Network) API. Two environments: prod `https://course.ntu.edu.tw/`, dev `https://course8pz3.aca.ntu.edu.tw/`.
- The relevant endpoint (confirmed via live OpenAPI spec fetch, dev env `https://course8pz3.aca.ntu.edu.tw/api/v3/api-docs/json`): `GET /api/v3/course-tables/result/:semester/:phase` (tag "Course Table", summary "取得使用者的選課結果"). Requires `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` — a token representing the specific student, NOT a service/admin credential. Path params: `semester` (e.g. `"114-2"`), `phase` (enum: PrePreReg, PreReg1, PreReg2, AddDrop1-6, Final — we should always use `Final` for "最終選課結果"). Query param `withCourse` (bool, include full course object). Response `ResultTable`: `{ assignedCourses: [{serial, course?, field, phase}], unassignedCourses: [{serial, course?, field, reason, phase}] }`. The nested `course` object's fields (id/serial/code/name/teacher/class/schedules/semester/etc.) line up with the existing `Course` entity's fields (Serial, CourseId=code, Name, TeacherId/TeacherName, Section=class, Semester).
- Local dev testing → use the dev course-network API. PRs merged into the `DeployTest` git branch → must use the PROD course-network API to fetch and store the real selection result. (Currently there is only ONE `NtuCourseApiOptions` config section in `src/FutureClassroom.Job/appsettings.json`, pointed at the dev host `course8pz3.aca.ntu.edu.tw`, and NO environment-specific override exists yet for it — `appsettings.Release.json` for the Job project currently only overrides `Ffmpeg.Path`. `.gitlab-ci.yml` shows `DeployTest` branch deploys with `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development` per `docker-compose.test.yml`, so simply relying on the standard ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT Development/Release split will NOT by itself give dev-vs-prod separation for this specific API — will likely need a distinct config key or env var override in the DeployTest docker-compose/CI, not just Release vs Development appsettings. Flag this to the user as something that needs a deploy-config decision, don't just silently assume.)
- Storage retention: keep only 3 semesters' worth of stored selection-result / enrollment data (oldest gets purged as new semesters are added).
- Semester naming: e.g. `114-2` — 114 is the academic year, `114-1` = fall semester, `114-2` = spring semester. The existing `Course.Semester` field stores it WITHOUT the dash as a 4-digit string (e.g. `"1142"`), and `CourseLessonSync.cs` has a private helper `ToApiSemester(string semester)` that converts `"1142"` → `"114-2"` for calling the NTU API — reuse this same convention for the new integration.
- Dev seed focus: 114-2 is the initial semester to support; 115-1's final result isn't published until 2026-09-25 17:00 (add/drop period ends then), so 115-1 data won't exist yet at implementation time.
- OAuth mechanism (confirmed by product owner): student authorizes on the frontend by being redirected through 新課程網's own login/OAuth flow, which internally ALSO uses NTU's institutional SAML SSO (the same IdP our own `/auth/login` uses). Because both apps trust the same IdP, once a student has an active NTU SSO session (from logging into FutureClassroom), being redirected to 新課程網's login will silently succeed (SSO chaining) without asking for credentials again — but it is still a SEPARATE token; our FutureClassroom session cookie cannot be reused to call the 新課程網 API directly. The frontend completes 新課程網's OAuth flow, obtains a bearer token, and POSTs that token to our backend. Exact registered OAuth client_id / authorize URL / redirect_uri / token exchange details are NOT YET KNOWN (no OAuth authorize/token endpoints for regular users were found in the dev OpenAPI spec — only admin-only endpoints `/api/v3/auth/admin/login` and `/api/v3/admin/token` exist there, which are unrelated). This is a genuine unresolved detail — the plan must surface it as an explicit open question/TODO for the user to provide, not invent fake endpoint URLs.

## Existing architecture facts gathered from direct code reading (all confirmed real, current):

### Backend data layer
- `src/FutureClassroom.Core/Data/AppDbContext.cs`: DbSets exposed as `public DbSet<T> Xs => Set<T>();`. `OnModelCreating` configures unique indexes (e.g. `Course.CourseKey` unique, `Lesson.LessonId` unique), FK via `HasPrincipalKey` when the FK references a non-PK column (Lesson→Course via CourseKey), composite keys via `e.HasKey(w => new { w.LessonId, w.WindowIndex })`, and `MaxLength` on strings.
- `Course` entity (`src/FutureClassroom.Core/Data/Course.cs`): Id(PK,int), CourseKey(unique, format `{semester}_{courseId}_{section}`), CourseId, Serial, Name, NameEn?, Semester, Section?, TeacherId, TeacherName, TotalStudentQuota, ClassroomName?, ClassroomLocation?, BuildingName?, BuildingId?, SchedulesJson?, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, `List<Lesson> Lessons`.
- `Lesson` entity: Id(PK), LessonId(unique, format `{courseKey}_{week}_{date}`), CourseKey(FK→Course.CourseKey), WeekNumber, LessonDate, Topic, Status("pending"/"analyzing"/"completed"), CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, `Course Course` nav.
- No enrollment/StudentCourse table exists at all today.
- Migrations live in `src/FutureClassroom.Api/Migrations/`, timestamp-prefixed (`{yyyyMMddHHmmss}_{PascalName}.cs`), simple `Up`/`Down` with `migrationBuilder.AddColumn<T>(...)` style calls. Most recent: `20260909231118_AddCourseNameEn.cs`.
- `src/FutureClassroom.Api/Services/CourseService.cs`: constructor-injected `AppDbContext db` (primary-constructor style, e.g. `public class CourseService(AppDbContext db)`), `GetCoursesAsync(string? semester)` builds `db.Courses.AsQueryable()`, filters, projects to DTOs, groups into a `CoursesResponse`. `src/FutureClassroom.Api/Services/DepartmentService.cs` is a smaller example of the same pattern (`AsNoTracking()`, `FirstOrDefaultAsync`, DTO projection).
- Services registered `AddScoped<T>()` in `src/FutureClassroom.Api/Program.cs`. DbContext registered via `AddDbContext<AppDbContext>` (not a factory) using `UseNpgsql(...)`.
- `src/FutureClassroom.Api/Endpoints/CourseEndpoints.cs` `GET /courses` currently returns ALL courses — has an explicit `// TODO: 之後要改成只能看到自己授課的課程` comment already in the code (phase-1 placeholder), never implemented.
- Auth: `src/FutureClassroom.Api/Endpoints/SsoEndpoints.cs` — `/auth/login`, `/auth/callback` (SAML), `/auth/logout`, `/auth/me`. After SAML callback succeeds, `SignInUserAsync(...)` builds claims (`ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier`=account, `ClaimTypes.Name`=name, `"StudentId"`=account, `"AccountSeq"`=seq, `"UserType"`=mapped role ("student"/"teacher"/"consultant"), `"Major"`=dept) and calls `context.SignInAsync(authScheme, new ClaimsPrincipal(identity))`. Cookie auth is configured in `Program.cs` with `options.ExpireTimeSpan = TimeSpan.FromHours(8)`, cookie name `_{baseUrlPath}`, `SameSite=None, Secure=true` for SAML-prefixed cookies via a custom `Saml2CookieManager`.
- Teacher's own `TeacherId` on `Course` comes from the NTU course API's `item.Teacher.Id` (an NTU account-like id) — should be comparable to the logged-in teacher's own `StudentId` claim (both ultimately NTU account identifiers), but this equivalence has NOT been empirically verified — flag as a thing to verify with real data during implementation.

### Job / Hangfire infrastructure
- `src/FutureClassroom.Job/Program.cs`: Hangfire configured with `UsePostgreSqlStorage()` pointing at the SAME Postgres connection string as the Api project (shared job storage). Recurring jobs registered via `recurringJobManager.AddOrUpdate<IXSync>("job-id", job => job.ExecuteAsync(), Cron.X())`. There is ALSO a demonstrated pattern for one-off/on-demand enqueue at startup: `var bootstrapClient = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IBackgroundJobClient>(); bootstrapClient.Enqueue<IDepartmentSync>(job => job.ExecuteAsync());`.
- Job interfaces are trivial: `Task ExecuteAsync()`, no params, decorated with `[DisplayName("...")]` (Hangfire dashboard label), some with `[DisableConcurrentExecution(300)]`. Implementations live in `src/FutureClassroom.Job/Jobs/Implement/`, e.g. `CourseLessonSync.cs`, `DepartmentSync.cs`. They inject `ILogger<T>`, `IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>` (note: Job project uses a DbContext FACTORY, unlike Api which uses plain AddDbContext), `IHttpClientFactory`, `IOptions<NtuCourseApiOptions>`.
- **Critical gap**: `FutureClassroom.Api` currently has ZERO Hangfire package reference and no `IBackgroundJobClient` registered. To let the Api project enqueue a job on student-login (requirement #2), Hangfire.Core (client-only, not server) needs to be added to Api's DI, pointed at the same Postgres storage, so it can call `backgroundJobClient.Enqueue<IEnrollmentSync>(j => j.ExecuteAsync(studentId, token))`. Since job parameters must be serializable by Hangfire (stored as job args in Postgres), passing a student's raw bearer token as a Hangfire job argument means it will be persisted in Hangfire's job-args storage in Postgres — flag this as a security consideration (token at rest in DB) for the plan to address (e.g., short-lived job argument, or store token encrypted/short-TTL row and pass only a reference id, not the raw token, as the Hangfire arg).
- HttpClient for NTU APIs is registered as a named client `"NTUCourseApi"` via `AddHttpClient("NTUCourseApi").ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(...)` (currently just a custom SSL validation callback, no auth header). No existing Bearer-token/DelegatingHandler pattern exists anywhere in the codebase — needs to be added fresh (e.g., pass the Bearer token as an explicit `Authorization` header per-request in the new job, simplest approach, no need for a DelegatingHandler since the token is per-student/per-call not static).
- `NtuCourseApiOptions` (`src/FutureClassroom.Job/Options/NtuCourseApiOptions.cs`) is a plain POCO bound via `services.Configure<NtuCourseApiOptions>(configuration.GetSection("NtuCourseApi"))`. Follow this same pattern for new selection-result-specific options (separate BaseUrl so dev/prod can be swapped independently of the existing course-search BaseUrl).

### Frontend
- `frontend/components/AuthProvider.tsx` calls `GET /auth/me` (via `apiFetch`) on mount; stores user in React Context; redirects unauthenticated users to `/login`.
- `frontend/app/login/page.tsx` calls `startSsoLogin()` (in `frontend/lib/api.ts`) which does `window.location.href = \`${API_BASE}/auth/login\``.
- `frontend/lib/api.ts`: central `apiFetch(path, init)` wrapper, auto-prepends `API_BASE` (`/api` in dev, `/futureclassroom/api` in prod), relies on same-origin cookie auto-inclusion (no explicit `credentials:'include'` needed), auto-redirects to login on 401.
- `frontend/app/api/[...path]/route.ts` is a Next.js API proxy route that forwards to the real backend and already correctly forwards 3xx redirects + cookies (relevant because an OAuth authorize redirect needs to flow through this proxy cleanly).
- `frontend/app/course/page.tsx`: fetches `GET /courses`, has an existing empty-state UI (with a help-ticket reference) for when no courses come back — useful pattern to reuse for "enrollment job still running" state.
- No existing `/callback`-style page exists yet, but `frontend/components/ShowcaseMode.tsx` demonstrates the codebase's established pattern for reading `URLSearchParams` from `window.location.search` and syncing state via `window.history.replaceState` — worth mirroring for an OAuth callback page.
- Env config: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH` exist in `.env.production`/`.env.local`/`.env.example`. New env vars would be needed for the 新課程網 OAuth client config once those details are known.

## What the plan needs to cover
Produce a concrete, staged implementation plan (not code) covering:
1. New DB schema: what table(s) to add (e.g. a `CourseSelectionResult` or `Enrollment` table keyed by StudentId+Semester+CourseKey, plus how "assigned" vs "unassigned/dropped" and the `Final` phase are represented), migration approach, and the 3-semester retention/purge strategy — where does the purge logic live (in the job itself? a separate cleanup step?).
2. New Options/config: what new Options class(es) and appsettings keys are needed for the selection-result API (separate dev/prod BaseUrl), and a concrete recommendation for how DeployTest-branch-uses-prod vs local-uses-dev should actually be wired given the ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT nuance described above (don't hand-wave this — give a specific mechanism: e.g. a new appsettings.DeployTest.json + corresponding ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT value threaded through docker-compose.test.yml and .gitlab-ci.yml, OR an explicit env-var override in the CI script — pick one and justify it).
3. New backend Job (`IEnrollmentSync` or similar) that, given a studentId + bearer token + semester, calls `GET /course-tables/result/{semester}/Final?withCourse=true` and upserts results into the new table.
4. How the Api project triggers this job right after a student's first login and how the raw student bearer token gets from an HTTP request into a Hangfire-enqueued job safely (address the token-at-rest concern above with a concrete recommendation).
5. New backend endpoint(s) needed for the frontend to POST the 新課程網 token to (e.g. `POST /auth/course-network-token`), and how "first login" is detected (e.g. check if a selection-result row already exists for that student+semester before enqueueing, vs a dedicated boolean flag).
6. Changes to `CourseEndpoints.GetCoursesAsync`/`CourseService` to filter courses: students → only CourseKeys present in their stored Final selection result for the current semester; teachers → only courses where `Course.TeacherId` matches their own identity (flag the unverified TeacherId≈StudentId assumption from above as something to confirm with real data, and suggest a fallback matching strategy, e.g. by name, in case IDs don't line up).
7. Frontend changes: where/how to trigger the 新課程網 OAuth redirect after normal login succeeds, a callback page to receive the token, wiring to POST it to the new backend endpoint, and how the course/analysis pages should behave while the sync job is still in flight (loading/empty state, reusing the existing empty-state pattern in `app/course/page.tsx`).
8. Explicit list of open questions/unknowns that MUST be confirmed with the product owner before implementation can start (the 新課程網 OAuth client_id/authorize URL/redirect_uri/token exchange details being the big one; also confirm exact "current semester" config source, and whether TeacherId in Course table actually matches the teacher's login StudentId).

Order the plan in implementable phases/stages (e.g. Phase A: DB schema + config; Phase B: backend job + token intake endpoint; Phase C: course filtering; Phase D: frontend OAuth flow) since this is a multi-week feature, not a single PR. For each phase note the concrete files to add/modify (paths, following the naming conventions observed above) and how to verify it end-to-end.

- `StudentId` (string, maxlength 32) — matches SSO `StudentId` claim
- `Semester` (string, maxlength 8) — 4-digit form, consistent with `Course.Semester`
- `CourseKey` (string, maxlength 64) — matches `Course.CourseKey` when resolvable; **nullable is not appropriate here since CourseKey is the join key** — instead store the raw `Serial`/`Field` from the API response as well, in case a returned course can't be matched to a locally-synced `Course` row yet (e.g., NTU API course not yet pulled in by `CourseLessonSync`). ## Phase B — Backend job (`IEnrollmentSync`) + token intake endpoint

**Goal:** given a studentId + 新課程網 bearer token + semester, fetch and store the Final selection result; wire the Api project to trigger this safely on first login.

**New job interface/impl** in `src/FutureClassroom.Job/Jobs/IEnrollmentSync.cs` + `src/FutureClassroom.Job/Jobs/Implement/EnrollmentSync.cs`, following `CourseLessonSync`'s constructor-injection pattern (`ILogger<EnrollmentSync>`, `IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>`, `IHttpClientFactory`, `IOptions<NtuCourseApiOptions>`). Signature: `Task ExecuteAsync(string studentId, string semester, string tokenReferenceId)` (NOT the raw token — see token-at-rest handling below). `[DisplayName("學生選課結果同步")]`, `[DisableConcurrentExecution(300)]` per-arg isn't directly supported by Hangfire out of the box for parameterized jobs, so rely on natural idempotency of the upsert instead (safe to run twice).

Steps inside `ExecuteAsync`:
1. Resolve the raw token from the reference id (see token storage below).
2. Build URL: `{SelectionResultBaseUrl}/{SelectionResultPath}/{ToApiSemester(semester)}/Final?withCourse=true` reusing the exact `ToApiSemester` helper convention from `CourseLessonSync.cs` (duplicate the private static method into a shared location — e.g. promote to `FutureClassroom.Core.Helpers.CourseHelper` since it's now needed in two Job classes, or just duplicate it identically if the team prefers not to touch `CourseHelper` yet — flag as a minor refactor decision).
3. `GET` with `Authorization: Bearer {token}` header set explicitly per-request via `HttpRequestMessage` (no DelegatingHandler needed, matches the existing codebase's lack of any auth-header abstraction).
4. Deserialize `ResultTable { assignedCourses: [...], unassignedCourses: [...] }` into DTOs matching the confirmed schema (`serial`, `course?`, `field`, `phase`, and `reason` for unassigned).
5. For each entry, resolve `CourseKey` by looking up `Courses` where `Serial == item.Serial && Semester == semester` (best-effort; leave null if not found yet).
6. 7. Run the 3-semester purge step (Phase A) at the end.
8. Delete the token reference row (one-time use) regardless of success/failure, to minimize token lifetime at rest.

**Token-at-rest handling (addresses the flagged security concern):** rather than passing the raw bearer token as a Hangfire job argument (which Hangfire persists as job args in Postgres, unencrypted, for the job's retention window), the Api project will:
1. On receiving the token via the new intake endpoint, generate a random opaque reference id (GUID).

3. Enqueue `IEnrollmentSync` with `(studentId, semester, referenceId)` — only the reference id touches Hangfire's persisted job-args table, never the raw token.
4. `EnrollmentSync` looks up and deletes the row by `ReferenceId` at the start of execution (single-use, decrypt via the same `IDataProtector`).
5. A cheap cleanup (either inline in `EnrollmentSync` or as part of the existing recurring job list) deletes any `PendingCourseNetworkToken` rows past `ExpiresAt` that were never consumed (e.g. job never ran) — small addition to the existing `CourseLessonSync`/new job's routine, or its own trivial recurring job registered at `Cron.Hourly()`.
